prompt: Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with concussion after a side impact at intersection. The patient had 6 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1041; do not mention it.)
text:
The patient presented following a side-impact motor vehicle collision at an intersection, reporting immediate headache, dizziness, transient disorientation, and sensitivity to light and noise. No loss of consciousness was reported at the scene, though the patient described brief confusion for several minutes afterward. Neurological examination on initial presentation showed a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15, with mild balance impairment on tandem gait and no focal motor or sensory deficits. Cervical strain was noted and managed concurrently.

Over six visits, management consisted of symptom monitoring, graduated return-to-activity guidance, vestibular and balance exercises, and reduction of screen exposure and cognitively demanding tasks during the acute phase. Symptoms improved steadily, with headache frequency and dizziness decreasing by the third visit. Balance testing normalized by the sixth visit, and the patient reported near-resolution of photosensitivity. Residual mild fatigue persists with prolonged concentration.

Prognosis is good with continued self-paced activity progression. The patient was advised to return promptly for any worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, or new weakness. Follow-up as needed is recommended.
